title: Non-Trend Strategies, Trader Flows, and Risk Management at DCM - Open Interest 11

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Non-Trend Strategies, Trader Flows, and Risk Management at DCM - Open Interest 11.docx

speakers: Jerome Callo (guest, founder DCM Systematic, ex-BlueTrend)
summary: Open Interest ep. 11 with DCM Systematic: a 25+ model non-trend multi-strategy fund built around behavioural flow anticipation (term structure, month end, shock overshoot, CTA positioning), relative value, and slow macro/cross-asset models, with proactive scenario risk management and a never-short-VIX rule. Sceptical that machine learning transfers directly to daily financial data.

coverage.note: teaser on risk system, intros, guest background (DCM Systematic, ex-BlueTrend)
why non-trend: orthogonal diversifier to CTA allocations; markets as supply/demand not just time series
three model families: behavioural flows, relative value, macro; anticipating carry traders via term structure
behavioural models holding 5-10 days; shock impulse overshoot models; risk parity de-risking flows
August 2024 yen carry unwind; consensus risk across 25 models and portfolio overlay; end-of-month flow effects
CTA positioning vs CFTC data; relative value; fast mean reversion on residuals of three-factor G10 FX model
stat-arb residuals; WTI vs Brent spread via term structure; limited neutrality
never short VIX, long vol bias; risk system uses stylised scenarios (Volmageddon)
proactive vs reactive risk; VIX asymmetry after Volmageddon; vol targeting acts as take-profit; retail short vol convexity
portfolio hedging research; macro bucket: slow inflation signals; FX carry risk-off neutralisation; ~19 independent degrees of freedom in 75 futures
cross-asset proxy for Brent via FX; 98% automation; ML role intro
why ML/LLMs struggle in finance: noisy learned signals, limited data, weak signal-to-noise, non-stationarity
sticky month-end effects vs decayed GSCI roll premium; moving target; outro

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: at any point in time you cannot be in a position that would put you out of business right you can control that
claims.claim: Risk management should ensure that no scenario can put the fund out of business, by listing what could go wrong (carry reversal, taper tantrum, oil shock) and adding each to the risk system.
claims.testable: partly - stress scenarios can be defined and tested

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: markets are not just a Time series but they are you know Supply and demands and all all kind of con straints
claims.claim: Mathematical models simplify a complex reality driven by supply, demand and constraints, so a single momentum driver is not enough and other approaches (relative value, behavioural models) can add return.

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: we should not overlap too much with uh Trend following programs because that part of the space is well covered by large Market participants
claims.claim: DCM deliberately avoids trend signals so its program is orthogonal to the CTA index and sits next to trend allocations in a broader portfolio.
claims.testable: yes - measure correlation to SG CTA index

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: is it easier to forast the market directly or to forecast certain Market participants that are using certain strategies
claims.claim: It may be easier to forecast the positioning of large systematic participants (carry, value, momentum, risk parity, trend) than to forecast the market, because they cannot unwind large positions quickly.
claims.direction: trade ahead of or against flows
claims.conditions: large managers need days to unwind
claims.testable: partly - needs proxies for participants' positions

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: looking at the term structure and uh typically trying to anticipate carry Traders while looking at the slope of ter structures on many instruments
claims.claim: Term-structure slope across futures lets one anticipate carry-trader repositioning, since a market does not flip between contango and backwardation overnight; models gauge the state and its evolution over a five to 10 day horizon.
claims.conditions: initially worked in FX and spread to other asset classes

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: give or take twice as fast as the thing you're trying to anticipate
claims.claim: A behavioural flow-anticipation model must be about twice as fast as the flow it tries to anticipate, giving a 5 to 10 day holding period and very low correlation to CTA indices.

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: what follows of a large shock like a Sigma shock on the commodity markets what do you see after that
claims.claim: After a large (two-sigma) shock, markets tend to overshoot and then normalise within about a week rather than continue, so shock impulse models fade the shock.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: billions of risk parity and Vault control trades sitting there that now need to get drisk because they're still long
claims.claim: After a sharp equity fall, risk-parity and vol-control funds must cut exposure as prices fall and volatility rises, creating selling flow that can be exploited for a few days.
claims.direction: short the flow then buy back
claims.conditions: vol-targeting funds long going into the shock
claims.testable: yes - event study after sigma shocks

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: we have an implementation of that principle that would try to keep a market neutrality across different indices
claims.claim: The shock-reversal model is run market-neutral across equity indices to limit directional risk, while other models handle vol spikes with long-volatility positioning.

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: it can happen that at time they are in a consensus view on on something right
claims.claim: With 25+ models the portfolio can end up with all models pointing the same way (e.g. the August 2024 yen carry unwind), so a portfolio-level overlay should cap aggregate directional, factor (carry) or risk-on exposure.

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: I tend to be surprised still by the end of month effects
claims.claim: End-of-month flow effects persist because large pools of capital rebalance on a monthly schedule, even though the inefficiency is documented.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: all of that leaves um skit marks in the markets which which you can exploit
claims.claim: Risk premia, factor and bank QIS strategies trade billions on rules and leave predictable footprints in prices that can be exploited.

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: you can have a a decent idea of okay how much do they represent
claims.claim: Scaling estimated trend and carry positioning to the whole CTA industry and comparing with CFTC net speculator/hedger positions shows how big crowded positions are, and the best opportunities arise when an over-traded position must unwind.
claims.indicator: estimated CTA positioning vs CFTC commitments
claims.testable: yes - CFTC data, CTA position estimate

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: you can explain L up to 80 90% of the variant um using a three Factor model
claims.claim: G10 FX returns versus USD are about 80 to 90% explained by three stable factors (all-vs-dollar, carry, Europe vs rest), a rare stationary stylised fact.
claims.indicator: three-factor model of G10 FX returns (dollar, carry, Europe)
claims.testable: yes - PCA of G10 FX returns

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: we have to play with the 10 15 person left of unexplained variance which is anything that is more ideosyncratic to a certain currency
claims.claim: After neutralising the known FX factors, the 10 to 15% idiosyncratic residuals are short-lived and mean revert over roughly 10 to 20 days, supporting a fast mean-reversion strategy.

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: if you impose a very strict Market neutrality there is some kind of overtrading happening or you have to leverage too much
claims.claim: Strictly market-neutral relative value (e.g. WTI vs Brent) forces overtrading or excessive leverage, so DCM allows slack and derives positions from term structure with a limited directional exposure.
claims.conditions: highly correlated pairs have little spread volatility

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: you what you can do is almost neutralize the the spot return risk using Brands to to offset whatever exposure you have to WTI spots
claims.claim: Pairing the steeper-backwardation contract with its neighbour neutralises spot risk while collecting roll-down yield, an RV carry construction.
claims.direction: long steeper backwardation, offset spot with the other

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: would um completely forbid the system the program to have a net short positioning on vix
claims.claim: The program never holds a net short VIX position, because its role is to provide diversification in drawdowns; it uses beta-adjusted VIX curve spreads and a fast model that goes long VIX when hedging demand rises.
claims.indicator: VIX futures curve; short-dated implied vol hedging demand
claims.direction: long VIX in shock risk; never net short

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: what could go spectacularly wrong with a certain asset class
claims.claim: Risk management should be proactive using stylised scenarios (e.g. Volmageddon shape: front VIX months hit most) injected into the optimiser as a loss constraint, rather than only scaling after realised volatility.
claims.testable: yes - scenario stress in the solver

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: proactive and reactive risk management
claims.claim: Proactive risk management stress-tests current positioning against past scenarios such as Volmageddon, while reactive risk management adjusts positions after the fact.
claims.testable: yes - stress test of current positions

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: the net pnl on that was plus three or plus 4% actually
claims.claim: On 6 Feb 2018 (Volmageddon) the DCM program, long the front of the VIX curve, still netted about +3 to +4% after giving some back the next day.
claims.indicator: long front VIX / short back VIX curve position

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: the book kind got got really reduced in exposure for couple of months or so and indeed um saved Capital saved the gains
claims.claim: Volatility-based risk management naturally cuts exposure after large gains (as in March 2020), working like automatic profit-taking and protecting capital.
claims.testable: yes - exposure vs realised vol after shocks

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: there are many Traders including retail Traders all around the world Expos exposed to short volatility trades
claims.claim: Many retail and other traders sit in short-volatility trades, so volatility shocks force liquidation and leave an exploitable convex footprint.

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: slower signals that are typically used on fixed income or FX uh thinking of inflation for instance
claims.claim: Macro models use inflation from CPI prints and from an in-house real-time nowcast built from equity sectors, giving holding periods of a month to a couple of months in fixed income and FX.
claims.indicator: inflation CPI and nowcast from equity sectors

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: a carry trade in effects would be hurt when there is a shock on the S&P 500
claims.claim: FX carry loses in equity risk-off shocks, so a regression-based risk-off factor is included in the risk system and neutralised in FX models.
claims.indicator: FX carry sensitivity to S&P 500 shocks
claims.testable: yes - regression beta to equity shocks

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: how many independent degrees of freedom do I really have in that in that pack you see it's more than it's more like 20 we've done the exercise I think couple of weeks ago and it was 19
claims.claim: A universe of about 75 futures contains only about 19 independent degrees of freedom, a compression that has grown since 2008 as markets became globally linked and liquidated together.
claims.indicator: effective number of independent bets (PCA) in 75 futures

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: let's try to get the best proxy of Brands using a bunch of currency pairs using you know some kind of robust regression techniques
claims.claim: A proxy for Brent built from currency pairs by robust regression (correlation about 0.5-0.6) lets a behavioural signal on Brent be traded through an FX basket, transferring signals across asset classes.
claims.indicator: Brent proxy from FX pairs via robust regression
claims.testable: yes - regression proxy and signal transfer

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: I would call that 98% automated in our case
claims.claim: Execution is 98% automated with pre-trade previews and manual send but no discretionary modification, with a human monitoring the process.

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: noisy version of something we know of like okay it's a risk premium it's a a car trade it's a momentum signal
claims.claim: Machine-learning models fitted to daily data usually recover a noisier version of known signals (risk premium, carry, momentum), so they add little beyond hand-built versions; higher-frequency data is more promising.
claims.testable: yes - compare learned vs engineered signal

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: in in finance we we don't have so much data
claims.claim: Financial data has far fewer observations than the parameters of modern AI models, and signal-to-noise is weak (e.g. an earnings surprise offset by a Fed cut), so models cannot disentangle effects.
claims.indicator: sample size and signal-to-noise for ML

claims.speaker: Jerome Callo
claims.quote: participants are changing the behaviors all the time
claims.claim: Markets lack stationarity because participants change behaviour and arbitrage away patterns, so patterns from 10 years ago may no longer hold, unlike protein folding rules.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: massive liquidity premium associated with um the earlier versions of the S&P gsci commodity index providing liquidity to that essentially roll window of business day 5 to9
claims.claim: The GSCI and DJ-UBS commodity index roll window (business days 5 to 9) once paid a large liquidity premium that has largely decayed as investors moved to smarter index implementations spreading roll across the curve.
claims.indicator: GSCI roll window, business days 5 to 9
claims.conditions: decayed after investors adopted smarter indices

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: it is human beings that run end of month accounting um and portfolio adjustments
claims.claim: Month-end effects are sticky because humans run month-end accounting and portfolio adjustments, unlike other anomalies that decay once published.
